heading: EXT. SALT FLAT - DEAD VEHICLE - DAY

units.text: EXT. SALT FLAT - DEAD VEHICLE - DAY
A white plain, blinding, cracked in hexagons to the horizon.
The heat has a sound.
A pickup truck sits dead on its rims with the hood propped open, and in its thin stripe of shade two figures sit side by side on the dirt.
IMOGEN STRAND, forties, sun-darkened, cracked lips, a scarf tied over her head, shreds a map into narrow strips and braids them.
Across from her, CALLUM REID, twenties, her nephew, with a gaze fixed so steady it has stopped meaning anything, turns a plastic bottle slowly, holding it up to the light.
Half a finger of water.
Maybe less.
Eleven miles to the highway. Maybe nine.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: Maybe.
units.name: CALLUM

units.text: She finishes the braid and ties it around his wrist without asking.
He lets her.
Should've turned at the cattle guard.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: He sets the bottle down between them, label facing her, a quiet gesture of an offer.
She pushes it back with one finger.
He pushes it again.
For a long moment neither of them speaks.
Then Imogen's eyes go past him, to the truck's rear bumper, and stay there.
A pale smear of damp in the dirt.
A slow, steady drip from under the truck.
Callum turns to look.
His face doesn't change.
His hand closes over hers.
It's the radiator.
units.name: CALLUM

units.text: It's the water tank, Cal. The tank was full.
units.name: IMOGEN

units.text: He gets up very slowly.
In the shade of the chassis, the second spare jug lies on its side, its cap cracked, empty.
